# Cladistics

```{r}
library("phangorn")
data = phyDat(data, type = "USER", levels = 0:10, ambiguity=NA)
```

## Neighbour-joining

Neighbour joining,
```{r}
dm <- dist.ml(data)
tree <- NJ(dm)
plot(tree, "unrooted", main="NJ unrooted tree")
Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, tree), similarity = TRUE)
results[,1] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, tree), similarity = TRUE)
```
```{r}
tree <- UNJ(dm)
plot(tree, "unrooted", main="UNJ unrooted tree")
results[,2] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, tree), similarity = TRUE)
```

## Maximum parsimony

```{r}
mm_start <- random.addition(data)
# Applying the pratchet method for maximum parsimony
# Default, fitch + SPR
mm_tree <- pratchet(data, start = mm_start, minit = 1000, maxit = 10000, all = TRUE, trace = 0, method = "fitch", rearrangements = "SPR", perturbation = "ratchet") # "The "fitch" algorithm only works correct for binary trees"
# Alternative
#mm_tree <- pratchet(data, start = mm_start, minit = 1000, maxit = 10000, all = TRUE, trace = 0, method = "sankoff", rearrangements = "SPR", perturbation = "ratchet")
```

```{r}
mm_tree
```

```{r}
parsimony(mm_tree, data)
```

```{r}
# Determining branch length
mm_tree <- acctran(mm_tree, data)
# Eliminating too short branches, to integrate polytomies/multifurcations
# we prune away internal edges of length tol (default = 1e-08), so our trees may contain multifurcations.
mm_tree  <- di2multi(mm_tree)
```

```{r}
# In case of several competing trees
#plot(consensus(mm_tree), "unrooted", main="Unrooted consensus tree")
#plotBS(mm_tree, type = "unrooted")
#plotBS(mm_tree)
plot(mm_tree, "unrooted", main="MP Unrooted tree")
results[,3] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, mm_tree), similarity = TRUE)
```

## Maximum likelihood

```{r}
# test only models that account for morphological-like data and fit them. No need to benchmark all this
init_tree = random.addition(data)
init_tree = NJ(dist.ml(data))
fit_mk <- pml(init_tree, data = data)
```

```{r}
fit_opt <- optim.pml(
  fit_mk, 
  optNni = TRUE,      # Optimize topology via NNI
  optEdge = TRUE,     # Optimize branch lengths
  optGamma = TRUE,    # Fit +G (Gamma rate variation across site variants)
  control = pml.control(trace = 0)
)

fit_opt
```

And now bootstrapping,

```{r}
# Bootstrap on the optimized Mk fit
bs <- bootstrap.pml(
  fit_opt, 
  bs = 100, 
  optNni = TRUE, 
  multicore = TRUE, 
  mc.cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1,
  control = pml.control(trace = 0)
)

# Plot results
plotBS(midpoint(fit_opt$tree), bs, p = 50, type = "p", main = "Mk Model Bootstrap")

# Quartet status comparison against ground truth
q_status <- Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, fit_opt$tree, nTip = TRUE)
results[, 4] <- Quartet::QuartetDivergence(q_status, similarity = TRUE)
```

## Bayesian methods (with Beast2)

Generate the Beast2 XML
```{r}
template_file <- "beast_templates/FBD_serial.xml"
out = "test"
xml_out = paste(out, ".xml", sep = "")
source("generate_beast.R")
generate_xml_from_template(
  phy_data          = data, 
  template_xml_path = template_file, 
  output_xml_path   = xml_out,
  chain_length      = 1000000#0
)
```

Now run:
```{r}
bin_folder = "/home/jbcamps/Data/F/Stemmatologie/bayesian/beast/bin/"
beast_bin <- paste(bin_folder, "beast", sep="")
system2(command = beast_bin, args = c("-overwrite", xml_out))
```



```{r}
log_file <- paste(out, ".log", sep = "")
# Use parse_beast_tracelog_file instead of parse_beast_output
log_data <- parse_beast_tracelog_file(log_file)
# Remove 10% burn-in using tracerer helper
log_no_burnin <- remove_burn_ins(log_data, burn_in_fraction = 0.1)
# Calculate ESS values for numeric parameters
ess_values <- calc_esses(log_no_burnin, sample_interval = 1000)
print(ess_values)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. Parse & Process Posterior Trees
# ==============================================================================
tree_file <- paste(out, "-dummyname.trees", sep="")

# Load NEXUS trees
trees <- ape::read.nexus(tree_file)

# Remove 10% burn-in manually
n_trees <- length(trees)
burnin_cutoff <- floor(0.1 * n_trees)
trees_after_burnin <- trees[(burnin_cutoff + 1):n_trees]


# ==============================================================================
# 3. Handle Sampled Ancestors in Consensus Trees
# ==============================================================================
## Generate a MCC to avoid the issues of consensus trees with internal nodes
treeannotator_bin <- paste(bin_folder, "treeannotator", sep="")
system(paste(treeannotator_bin, "-burnin 10 -height median", tree_file, "mcc_tree.tree"))
```

```{r}
# Read the MCC tree with annotations preserved
mcc_tree <- read.nexus("mcc_tree.tree")
plot(mcc_tree, main = "Maximum Clade Credibility Tree")
write.tree(mcc_tree, file = "", append = FALSE,
           digits = 2, tree.names = TRUE)
Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, mcc_tree, nTip = TRUE), similarity = TRUE)
```





```{r}
library(babette)
# Create the necessary fasta format
write.phyDat(data, "tmp", format="fasta")#, type="USER")


# 2. Configure the inference model
# For non-DNA discrete data, specify the Lewis Mk site model
inference_model <- create_inference_model(
  site_model = create_jc69_site_model(gamma_site_model = create_gamma_site_model(gamma_cat_count = 4)), # Sort of Mk model
  clock_model = create_strict_clock_model(),   # Strict vs Relaxed clock
  tree_prior  = create_yule_tree_prior(),      # Birth-death or Yule prior
  mcmc        = create_mcmc(chain_length = 10000, store_every = 1000)
)

# 3. Run BEAST2 directly from R
out <- bbt_run_from_model("tmp",
                          inference_model = inference_model
)

# 4. Process the outputs returned directly into R memory:
# - Posterior trees (ape multiPhylo object)
posterior_trees <- out$my_variants_trees

# - MCMC parameter log (data.frame)
mcmc_log <- out$estimates
```


```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Extract Results & Post-Processing
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Check MCMC Convergence / ESS (aim for ESS > 200)
clean_log <- tracerer::remove_burn_ins(out$estimates, burn_in_fraction = 0.1)
ess_table <- tracerer::calc_esses(clean_log, sample_interval = 1000)
print(ess_table)

# 2. Extract Posterior Trees (ape multiPhylo object)
# Note: babette labels the list element using the temp file's name
tree_name <- names(out)[grep("_trees$", names(out))]
posterior_trees <- out[[tree_name]]

# 3. Compute 50% Majority-Rule Consensus Tree
burnin <- floor(0.1 * length(posterior_trees))
trees_after_burnin <- posterior_trees[(burnin + 1):length(posterior_trees)]
consensus_tree <- phangorn::consensus(trees_after_burnin, p = 0.5)

# 4. Plot Consensus Tree with Posterior Probabilities
plotBS(
  tree = consensus_tree, 
  trees = trees_after_burnin, 
  type = "phylogram", 
  main = "Bayesian Consensus Tree (Lewis Mk Model)"
)
```




## Distance scoring

### Topology only
Quartet::QuartetStatus(tree1, tree2) or TreeDist::TripletDistance(tree1, tree2)

Recommendation for Benchmarking Scripts:
Report both metrics in parallel. Generalized RF gives you the global structural accuracy score, while Quartet gives you the fine-grained local relationship score.

### With branch lengths

Kendall-Colijn (KC) Metric:What it does: Represents each rooted tree as a vector encoding the distance from the root to the Most Recent Common Ancestor (MRCA) of every pair of tips. A weight parameter $\lambda \in [0, 1]$ smoothly transitions the metric between pure topology ($\lambda = 0$) and topology weighted by branch length ($\lambda = 1$).Pros/Cons: Exceptional for rooted genealogies and phylodynamics.

R Implementation: treespace::treeDist(tree1, tree2, lambda = 0.5) or TreeDist::KendallColijn(tree1, tree2).

Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann (BHV) Geodesic Distance:What it does: Measures the shortest continuous path through continuous "tree space" accounting for topology shifts and edge lengths.
R Implementation: distory::dist.multiPhylo(c(tree1, tree2)).
